why: Give each appended rating a fixed slot in arrival order. A max segment tree over slots answers 'largest rating, leftmost slot', and deleted slots are set to minus infinity. A Fenwick tree of alive flags converts between a current index and a slot: the current index of a slot is the number of alive slots before it, and deleting index k means finding the (k+1)-th alive slot.
hints: Deletion shifts indices, but the relative order of survivors never changes. What if every rating keeps the slot where it was appended?
Two jobs: (1) map current index <-> slot under deletions, which is order-statistics on an alive bitmap; (2) find the leftmost maximum among alive slots.
Fenwick tree over alive flags (prefix count, and binary-lifting search for the k-th alive slot) plus a max segment tree that descends left on ties. Each operation O(log n).
pitfalls: The query must return the earliest current index among equal maxima, after converting the slot back to a shifted index.
Deleting from a Python list and scanning for the max is O(n) per operation and too slow at scale.
Mark deleted slots as minus infinity in the segment tree, not 0, in case ratings can be 0 or negative.
statement:
Start with an empty list of employee ratings and process operations in order:

  • [1, rating]: append rating to the end of the list.
  • [2, index]: delete the rating at zero-based position index; later ratings shift one place left. The index is always valid.
  • [3]: report [maxRating, earliestIndex], the largest rating in the list and the smallest current index holding it. Queries are made only while the list is non-empty.

Return the answers of all type-3 operations, in order.

Worked example: [[1,5],[1,7],[1,7],[3],[2,1],[3]]

  • After three appends the list is [5, 7, 7].
  • Query: max is 7, first at index 1, so output [7, 1].
  • Delete index 1: list becomes [5, 7].
  • Query: max 7 at index 1, so output [7, 1].
  • Answer: [[7,1],[7,1]].
constraints:
• Not stated in the source; reasonable bounds: 1 ≤ operations.length ≤ 2 * 10^5
  • 0 ≤ rating ≤ 10^9
  • Every delete index is valid; queries happen only on a non-empty list
